touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf. The gates are CodeMother's (9.3.5).

A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf (Akien, same day: "that could be in the class, rather than the instance :) self queuing"). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10: "now it has to send it's fileref over to the thing that will process it, and a new code instance created over there even tho it's the same thing... because that's good encapsulation. :)"
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A diagnostic report, EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.

A trouble has a point of origin, and that is how they match: when raised, its emission source AND error message are checked against the open tickets. If found, increment; either way, pass the ticket back to the caller.
So the error a raiser reports is the same words every time; whatever changes from one time to the next (a pid, a timestamp, a temp path) goes in the details, not the error.

conflicts.text: A trouble has a point of origin, and that is how they match: when raised, its emission source AND error message are checked against the open tickets. If found, increment; either way, pass the ticket back to the caller.
conflicts.ticket_says: Error message varies with each refusal reason (e.g. 'holder refused it: component base reds the build_inspector')
conflicts.why: Outline says troubles are matched by 'emission source AND error message'. Variable error messages prevent matching/incrementing of repeated refusals of the same ticket by the same gate.

conflicts.text: So the error a raiser reports is the same words every time; whatever changes from one time to the next (a pid, a timestamp, a temp path) goes in the details, not the error.
conflicts.ticket_says: Error includes variable refusal reason details in the message itself: '<holder> refused it: <first line of reason>'
conflicts.why: Outline states 'the error a raiser reports is the same words every time' and 'whatever changes from one time to the next (a pid, a timestamp, a temp path) goes in the details, not the error'. This principle maintains error consistency for matching. Variable reasons violate it.
